quarterly_data.quarter: NVIDIA press release: NVIDIA and Cisco Introduce New Pluggable Optics Form Factor (10-12-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: NVIDIA and Cisco announced plans (at OCP) for Ultra-Dense Small Form Factor Pluggable (USFP), a new high-density 400Gb/s-per-lane optical module for pluggable transceivers, which the companies say is designed to be the first module to support 400Gb/s-per-lane electrical signals. The first planned USFP-based transceivers pack 16 full-duplex lanes in an OSFP-sized footprint supporting both switches and SuperNICs, with the ability to expand to 32 and more lanes; customers will be able to achieve 12.8Tb/s of overall capacity. Versus 200Gb/s-per-lane pluggable modules it delivers 4x the bandwidth and front-panel bandwidth density with approximately 1.3x the power efficiency, and supports power dissipation of up to 100 watts without a separate embedded cooling circuit. NVIDIA and Cisco are collaborating with TE Connectivity and Amphenol to build USFP cages, connectors and modules, with additional partners expected to join, and plan an open industry specification through an upcoming community-led multi-source project. No availability date was stated.
quarterly_data.figure: 400Gb/s per lane; 16 lanes (expandable to 32); 12.8Tb/s; 4x bandwidth density; ~1.3x power efficiency; up to 100 watts
